- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model consistently underestimates true values in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a small upward bias for early days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day average), model often overshoots in the immediate next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below the peak or adjust downward based on sentiment decay.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not be too aggressive in reversing; allow gradual recovery.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error; when sentiment shifts sharply, model should lag by 1–2 days in adjusting forecast direction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period (last 7–10 days) true values; apply a “late-stage correction” rule: if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in last 7 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
